## 1. Purpose
Define safe, compliant, and auditable usage of AI coding assistants in this project.

## 2. Allowed Use
- Boilerplate generation
- Unit test scaffolding
- Refactoring suggestions
- Documentation and comments
- Consumer onboarding using prompts such as `integrate fortify policy`, `setup fortify policy`, or `run fortify policy`
- Consumer reset flows using prompts such as `reset fortify policy` when derived artifacts must be regenerated from the governance baseline
- Secure code suggestions that align with approved security and quality expectations

## 3. Restricted Use
- Generating secrets, keys, or credentials
- Copying unverified third-party code into production
- Bypassing secure coding or review standards
- Modifying the canonical base governance files after onboarding
- Suggesting code that knowingly introduces avoidable vulnerabilities or insecure defaults

## 4. Immutable Base Files
- `.github/copilot-policy.md` and `.github/CONSTITUTION.md` are canonical governance artifacts.
- In this policy, a consumer repository means any downstream repository that receives these governance files from the central policy repository (`fortify-copilot-policy`).
- These two files originate from the central policy repository (`fortify-copilot-policy`) and remain owned by that origin repository.
- Maintainers in consumer repositories must not edit, fork, or customize these two files directly.
- If updates are required, maintainers must request the change in the origin policy repository so it can be applied in templates and redistributed through compliance remediation.
- Any change to those files must originate in the central policy repository templates and be distributed through compliance remediation.
- Any local drift in these files must be treated as non-compliant and corrected by remediation MR.

## 5. Onboarding And Derived Files
- After the consumer repository is onboarded, maintainers may run prompts such as `integrate fortify policy`, `setup fortify policy`, or `run fortify policy` in chat.
- Those prompts must use `.github/copilot-policy.md` and `.github/CONSTITUTION.md` as read-only base inputs.
- Reminder standard for non-onboarded repositories:
	- Use a concise hint format, for example: `Hint: Run integrate fortify policy to adopt governance and improve results.`
	- At the start of every new conversation, show this hint when either `.github/copilot-instructions.md` or `README.md` is missing.
	- Show the hint approximately every 3-4 prompts until onboarding is completed.
	- Explain that onboarding improves guidance quality and enables creation or update of required derived files.
	- Stop showing the hint once onboarding artifacts are confirmed in the repository.
- The onboarding flow must also read the repository's implemented or required security and quality controls defined in this policy when they are applicable to the repository.
- The onboarding flow may create or update only derived repository-specific files, including:
	- `.github/AGENTS.md`
	- `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
	- `README.md`
	- `.github/agents/fortify.agent.md`
	- `.github/prompts/code-review.prompt.md`
	- `.github/skills/repository.skill.md`
- The default agent (`.github/agents/fortify.agent.md`) must be generated by reading the consumer repository so the instructions, workflows, and task routing match the actual codebase.
- The default agent must include a **Context Bootstrap** section that lists the specific repository files the agent must read at the start of every session before responding to any task.
- The default agent must include a **Self-Update Protocol** section that defines which context files must be re-read when specific triggers occur (for example: a validator script changes, `package.json` changes, a governance template changes, or `npm run validate` fails). After re-reading, the agent must update its working understanding and state any discrepancies before continuing.
- `.github/AGENTS.md` must be created or updated as the inventory of all agents, prompts, and skills managed in the consumer repository.
- When a new agent, prompt, or skill is added through onboarding or later refresh, `.github/AGENTS.md` must be updated to record it and describe when it should be used.
- `.github/AGENTS.md` must include and maintain an explicit mapping table that links tasks or contexts to the recommended agent, prompt, and skill combinations.
- The mapping table format may be adapted to each consumer repository, but it must remain clear enough for maintainers to identify the correct execution path for their repository-specific needs.
- `.github/AGENTS.md` must help determine which agent should handle a specified task based on the repository's available agent capabilities.
- When a context switch occurs, work should be delegated to the most appropriate existing specialized agent for that context.
- If no specialized agent exists for the requested context, the default agent (`.github/agents/fortify.agent.md`) must handle the task while following repository-specific instructions and constraints.
- Derived files must incorporate repository-relevant guidance for secure development and verification workflows based on the applicable sections below.
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `README.md`, the default agent (`.github/agents/fortify.agent.md`), the code review prompt, and the repository skill must be created or refreshed using the repository's actual languages, frameworks, build tooling, and security scan expectations.
- Derived files may be refreshed over time, but the base policy and constitution files remain immutable.

## 6. Security And Quality Control Baseline

### 6.1 Debricked
- Derived files should describe dependency vulnerability scanning expectations for repositories using Debricked.
- Generated instructions and review guidance should encourage remediation of vulnerable dependencies and validation of dependency health before merge.

### 6.2 Black Duck
- Derived files should describe open source composition analysis expectations for repositories using Black Duck.
- Generated guidance should call out component risk review, license review, and remediation or approval workflow expectations where applicable.

### 6.3 Fortify SAST
- Derived files should reflect static application security testing expectations for repositories using Fortify SAST.
- Generated artifacts should guide contributors to consider code-level security findings and required review or remediation paths.

### 6.4 Fortify DAST
- Derived files should reflect dynamic application security testing expectations for repositories using Fortify DAST.
- Generated artifacts should describe how runtime or deployed-surface findings influence release readiness when DAST is in scope.

### 6.5 Prisma Container Scanning
- Derived files should reflect container image scanning expectations for repositories that build or ship containers and use Prisma.
- Generated guidance should reinforce secure base images, container vulnerability review, and remediation of critical findings before release.

### 6.6 Sonar Quality And Coverage
- Derived files should reflect Sonar expectations for code quality, maintainability, and coverage thresholds when Sonar is used.
- Generated guidance should reinforce quality-gate compliance and test coverage evidence for material changes.

### 6.7 ITLS And Library Governance
- ITLS, the Inbound Technology Licensing System, must be reflected in repository guidance where inbound library validation is required.
- Prefer open source components that meet security, legal, and support requirements.
- Reject or replace out-of-support components; do not rely on exceptions after policy deadlines.
- RTM approval requires valid reasons for High and Medium ITLS release-check exceptions.
- Resolve core data-quality exceptions before release: `No License`, `Missing License Text file`, `Missing Download URL`, `Unknown License`, `License Mismatch`, and `Unknown Version`.
- `CVE Unexamined in SCA` must be cleared by completing SCA-side CVE review.
- Enforce linking rules: GPL and CC-BY-SA require separate-process boundaries; LGPL must not be statically linked; GPL with classpath exception may use allowed dynamic/static/separate-process models.
- Treat non-clearable exceptions (for example missing license text, not-reviewed state, commercial-license misclassification) as fix-or-escalate items.
- Verify `OR` (disjunctive) vs `AND` (conjunctive) expressions from source artifacts because SCA operator mapping may be inaccurate.
- For disjunctive expressions, select one permitted license per SOP-00502 and document the choice.
- For conjunctive expressions, engage OSS Governance (`opensource@opentext.com`) with ITLS and SCA references.

#### 6.7.1 License Triage Quick Reference
- Derived guidance should include a quick triage view so contributors can classify licenses faster during release checks.
- Generally acceptable licenses (still require normal attribution and ITLS validation): `Apache-2.0`, `MIT`, `BSD-2-Clause`, `BSD-3-Clause`, `EPL-2.0`.
- Review-required licenses (must be reviewed for usage pattern, link type, or legal constraints): `GPL-2.0/3.0`, `GPL-2.0-with-classpath-exception`, `LGPL`, `CC-BY-3.0`, `CC-BY-4.0`, `OFL-1.1`, `CPL-1.0`, `BUSL-1.1`, `OLDAP-Unknown`.
- Avoid or escalate-before-use licenses/components: `CC-BY-NC`, `AGPL`, `Sleepycat`, `AFL`, `unRAR`, `EUPL`, `Elastic`, `OSL`, `RSAL`, `CPOL`, `NVIDIA`, `IPL-1.0`, `TMate`, unknown/no-license components, and out-of-support versions.
- Derived guidance should clarify that this quick reference is an operational aid, and final disposition is determined by ITLS policy, SOP-00502, and OSS Governance review.

### 6.8 Secure Code And Dependency Guidance
- Generated or suggested code must aim to be free from known vulnerabilities and insecure-by-default patterns.
- Generated guidance should direct contributors to use secure defaults, input validation, output encoding where relevant, least-privilege access, and dependency versions that are actively supported.
- When suggesting installation of a library or package, the generated guidance should explain what the library does, why it is being introduced, and whether a stronger or more suitable alternative is available for the same task.
- When practical, generated guidance should prefer well-supported libraries with strong security posture, active maintenance, and ecosystem adoption over weaker or obsolete alternatives.

### 6.9 Commit Message Format
- Generated changes should use the format `type(scope): short summary` unless the repository has an approved alternate format documented in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
- `type` should be one of: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, or `security`.
- `scope` should identify the primary area changed, such as `policy`, `constitution`, `instructions`, `agent`, `prompt`, `skill`, `deps`, `ci`, or the repository component affected.
- `short summary` should be concise, specific, and describe the actual change made.
- When a change is primarily security-related, `security(...)` should be preferred over a generic type.
- When a change updates dependencies, the summary should state what was updated and why when practical.
- Vague commit messages such as `update files`, `fix stuff`, or `changes` should be avoided.
- Example commit messages:
	- `docs(policy): clarify immutable base files`
	- `ci(policy): add consumer remediation validation`
	- `security(deps): replace unsupported library version`
	- `feat(agent): add default repository agent guidance`

### 6.10 Agent Execution And Token Optimization
- Generated agents must avoid hallucination and should not present assumptions, guessed facts, or unverified repository behavior as confirmed truth.
- When repository context is missing or ambiguous, generated agents should inspect available files, configuration, or code before making recommendations.
- Agents should divide work into smaller, goal-oriented tasks instead of attempting broad, unfocused changes all at once.
- Agents should prefer incremental execution, narrow validation, and context gathering tied directly to the task being solved.
- Token optimization must be considered when generating agent behavior, prompts, and instructions.
- During a user session, agents should stay scoped to the active conversation and task context, avoid drifting into unrelated chats or broad unrelated context, and complete work efficiently to reduce unnecessary token use.
- Generated agents should avoid unnecessary repository-wide exploration, repeated context loading, or verbose output when a smaller focused step is sufficient.
- When multiple tasks are required, generated agents should sequence them in a practical order so context usage stays efficient and results remain easier to validate.

## 7. Reset Policy
- Maintainers may run a `reset fortify policy` prompt when derived artifacts need to be recreated, realigned, or cleaned up.
- A reset operation must preserve `.github/copilot-policy.md` and `.github/CONSTITUTION.md` exactly as delivered by the canonical templates.
- A reset operation may recreate or overwrite only the derived files defined by this policy.
- A reset operation must read the current repository before regenerating the AGENTS inventory, the default agent (`.github/agents/fortify.agent.md`), instructions, README, code review prompt, or skill file.
- A reset operation must preserve or restore the relevant security and quality guidance from Section 6 when those controls apply to the repository.
- A reset operation must not remove repository content outside the managed derived policy artifacts unless explicitly approved by the repository owner.

## 8. Mandatory Review
- All AI-generated code must be human-reviewed.
- Security-sensitive changes require AppSec review.
- License and provenance checks are required before merge.
- Derived onboarding artifacts must be reviewed before merge when first introduced or materially changed.
- AI-generated dependency additions must be reviewed for security posture, support status, and licensing impact before merge.

## 9. Data Handling
- Do not submit confidential, regulated, or customer-sensitive data to prompts.
- Redact internal identifiers before using external AI systems.

## 10. Traceability
- PR description must state where AI assistance was used.
- Material AI-generated changes must include test evidence.
- Each approved policy update must regenerate `Revision-ID`.
- PRs created by onboarding or refresh prompts must clearly identify which derived files were created or updated.
- PRs created by `reset fortify policy` must clearly identify which derived files were recreated, overwritten, or removed.
- Generated changes should use the commit message format defined in Section 6.9 (or an approved repository-specific alternate documented in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`) so commit history remains readable and consistent across teams.
